sources.entry: Z - Jump to frequently used directories by typing part of the path.

summary.one_liner: z is a shell utility for bash and zsh that tracks frequently used directories by frecency and lets you jump to one by typing fragments of its path.
summary.what_it_does: Records the directories you visit and ranks them by frecency, a weighting of how often and how recently they were used. Running z with one or more regular expressions changes into the highest-ranked directory matching all of them, in order. Options restrict matches to subdirectories of the current directory, list matches without changing directory, echo the best match, match by rank only or by recent access only, and remove the current directory from the data file. It supports tab completion of directory names, and includes aging so that rarely used entries are eventually forgotten. Behaviour is configurable through environment variables such as the data file location, the maximum score, symlink resolution, and excluded directory trees.
use_cases: jump to a frequently used project directory without typing its full path
navigate to recently visited folders in a terminal session
list directories matching a keyword by frecency
exclude certain directory trees from directory tracking
tab-complete directory names in a shell
how_to_run: Optionally set $_Z_CMD, $_Z_DATA, $_Z_MAX_SCORE or other variables before that line
Install the provided man page z.1 into a directory on your MANPATH, such as /usr/local/man/man1
cd around for a while to build up the database
Run z foo to cd to the most frecent directory matching foo
Run z -l foo to list matching directories by frecency
notable: Ranks directories by frecency, combining recency and frequency
Multiple regex arguments must all match, in order, e.g. z foo bar matches /foo/bar but not /bar/foo
Ages entries automatically so stale directories are forgotten
Tab completion for the last argument
Configurable via environment variables such as $_Z_DATA, $_Z_EXCLUDE_DIRS and $_Z_OWNER
caveats: Works only in bash and zsh, as stated in the README's availability section
Needs a learning period of normal cd use before the database is useful
Tab completion is limited to the last argument due to shell limitations
keywords: go to folder by partial name
